questions.q: What does the with statement guarantee when opening a file?
options: The file can never be opened in write mode
The file is automatically deleted after reading
The file is automatically converted to CSV format
The file gets closed automatically when the block ends, even if an error happens inside it
questions.explain: This is Python's context manager pattern — it removes the risk of forgetting to close a file, including on error paths.

questions.q: What is the difference between 'w' and 'a' file modes?
options: 'w' overwrites the file completely if it exists; 'a' appends to the end without erasing existing content
'a' deletes the file; 'w' creates a backup
'w' can only be used with numbers, 'a' only with text
'w' and 'a' are identical in every way
questions.explain: Choosing the wrong mode can silently erase data you meant to keep.

questions.q: Why does iterating a file with 'for line in f' matter for large files?
options: It automatically sorts the file's contents
It has no practical benefit over any other method
It reads one line at a time instead of loading the whole file into memory at once
It converts the file to Parquet format
questions.explain: This line-by-line approach avoids memory problems on files too large to load all at once.

questions.q: Why does this lesson matter even though Lesson 21's pandas.read_csv() handles file mechanics automatically?
options: Understanding what's happening underneath matters the moment something goes wrong — an encoding error, a file that won't close, a memory issue on a huge file
Pandas cannot actually read CSV files at all
This lesson's content becomes completely irrelevant after Lesson 21
Pandas requires manually opening files first in every case
questions.explain: Chapter 4's PySpark write operations are also built on this same open-write-close idea, just distributed across a cluster.

questions.q: What does .strip() do when reading a line from a file?
options: Deletes the line entirely
Splits the line into a list of characters
Converts the line to uppercase
Removes the trailing newline character from the line
questions.explain: Lines read from a file include a trailing newline that strip() removes before further processing, like splitting on commas.
